docs.badge.a11y.change: A badge that changes while the page is open is not announced. If the change matters, tell the user in a live region, or in the text of the control that caused it.
docs.badge.a11y.contrast: Each tone pairs a text color with its own background, and both are defined for the light and the dark theme. A color of your own through className is yours to check.
docs.badge.a11y.native: It is a span with no role of its own, so a screen reader reads its text in the flow of the page, next to the item it tags.
docs.badge.a11y.text: Color is never the only thing that says what a badge means. Write the status in the text («Failed»), and use the tone to reinforce it.
docs.badge.api.children: The text of the badge, which is what says what it means. Keep it to a word or two.
docs.badge.api.className: Added after the library's own class names.
docs.badge.api.others: Every other attribute of the native span element goes to it as it is: id, title, role, aria-*, data-*, the event handlers and ref.
docs.badge.api.tone: The color role of the badge. It colors the badge and says nothing by itself: its text must say the same thing.
docs.badge.limit.interactive: A badge is not a button or a link: it has no hover, focus or dismiss behavior. Put an interactive control next to it when it needs one.
docs.badge.limit.size: There is one size and no icon slot. A badge is text.
docs.badge.limit.tones: There are five tones and no way to add one: a status that none of them fits takes the neutral one, and its text says the rest.
docs.badge.limit.wrap: The text never wraps, so a long one makes the badge wider than a narrow container. Keep it short.
docs.badge.summary: A short label that tags an item with a status or a category.
docs.badge.tones.description: Five color roles for a badge. Each one is shown on a card, because the neutral badge has the background of the panel.
docs.badge.tones.title: Tones
docs.badge.usage.description: Import Badge and write the status in its text. The tone only colors the badge: the word is what says what it means.
docs.button.a11y.disabled: Use disabled for an action that is not available at all: the button leaves the tab order. Use aria-disabled when it must stay focusable, and say why it is unavailable.
docs.button.a11y.focus: The focus ring shows with the keyboard and is never removed. Keep it visible if you restyle the button.
docs.button.a11y.loading: While loading, the button is aria-busy and aria-disabled, shows the loading label and stays in the tab order, so a keyboard user does not lose their place.
docs.button.a11y.name: Its content is its accessible name. Write what the action does («Save draft»), not «Click here». An icon alone needs IconButton, which requires a label.
docs.button.a11y.native: It is a native button element: Enter and Space activate it, and it takes part in forms.
docs.button.a11y.state: State is never shown by color alone: loading changes the text and adds a spinner, and a disabled button is announced as unavailable.
docs.button.a11y.target: The button is 44 px high on a touch screen.
docs.button.api.ariaBusy: Native: set while the button is loading.
docs.button.api.ariaDisabled: Native: the button is announced as unavailable but keeps the focus. Button sets it while loading, and it does not stop clicks by itself.
docs.button.api.block: Makes the button fill the width of its container.
docs.button.api.children: The content of the button, which is its accessible name.
docs.button.api.className: Added after the library's own class names.
docs.button.api.icon: Name of an icon shown before the content. A spinner takes its place while the button is loading.
docs.button.api.loading: Ignores clicks and shows loadingLabel while an action runs. The button stays focusable.
docs.button.api.loadingLabel: Content that replaces the button's own while it is loading, and so its accessible name. Without it the button uses the buttonLoading string of the closest FormaProvider, or «Loading…».
docs.button.api.onClick: Called on a click. It is not called while the button is loading.
docs.button.api.others: Every other attribute of the native button element goes to it as it is: disabled, name, value, form, aria-*, data-*, the event handlers and ref.
docs.button.api.type: Set to button so that a button inside a form does not submit it by accident.
docs.button.limit.ariaDisabled: An aria-disabled button looks like a default one except for its cursor, and it still calls onClick: ignore the click yourself and explain why it is unavailable.
docs.button.limit.link: To style a link as a button use buttonClassName. The link keeps its own semantics.
docs.button.limit.loadingLabel: The loading text comes from a FormaProvider or from loadingLabel. Without either it is «Loading…», in English.
docs.button.limit.pressed: A pressed (active) state is not painted.
docs.button.limit.size: There is one height. The sizes of the design are a proposal and have no prop.
docs.button.sizes.description: The library has one height. The other sizes are a proposal.
docs.button.sizes.note: Proposed scale: the library has no size prop, so these buttons are disabled and have no JSX. Button is {regular, number} px high, and {touch, number} px below 768 px.
docs.button.state.focusHint: Reach it with Tab: a ring appears around it.
docs.button.state.hoverHint: Move the pointer over it: the primary button darkens.
docs.button.states.description: The states that Button has today. Each one is a different thing: a disabled button is not a loading one.
docs.button.states.note: There is no pressed state: the library paints nothing for an active button yet.
docs.button.summary: Variants, states and proposed sizes of an action.
docs.button.usage.description: Import Button and give it a name that says what the action does. It is type="button" unless you set it.
docs.button.variants.description: Four levels of emphasis for an action. Use one primary action for each view.
docs.iconButton.a11y.disabled: A disabled button leaves the tab order and is announced as unavailable. If it has to stay focusable, say why it is unavailable next to it.
docs.iconButton.a11y.focus: The focus ring shows with the keyboard and is never removed. Keep it visible if you restyle the button.
docs.iconButton.a11y.name: The icons are hidden from screen readers and the label names the button, so write what the action does («Add a client»), not what the icon looks like («Plus»).
docs.iconButton.a11y.native: It is a native button element: Enter and Space activate it, and it takes part in forms.
docs.iconButton.a11y.target: The button is a square of 44 px, the size of a finger, at every width.
docs.iconButton.a11y.tooltip: Sighted users cannot read a label that is not on the screen: wrap the button in a Tooltip with the same text. Then set describe='{false}' on the Tooltip, or a screen reader says the name twice.
docs.iconButton.api.ariaLabel: Native: set from label. A value of your own is overwritten.
docs.iconButton.api.className: Added after the library's own class names.
docs.iconButton.api.flip: Mirrors the icon horizontally, so one drawing serves two directions. It is a mirror and not a rotation.
docs.iconButton.api.icon: Name of the icon to draw, or a list of names to draw side by side, overlapping, as one glyph. The names may repeat.
docs.iconButton.api.label: The accessible name of the button. It is required: the button has no visible text, so without it a screen reader has nothing to say.
docs.iconButton.api.others: Every other attribute of the native button element goes to it as it is: disabled, onClick, name, form, aria-*, data-*, the event handlers and ref. It takes no children: the icon is drawn from icon.
docs.iconButton.api.type: Set to button so that a button inside a form does not submit it by accident.
docs.iconButton.icons.description: One icon, several icons drawn as a single glyph such as a double arrow, and the same glyph mirrored with flip.
docs.iconButton.icons.title: Icons
docs.iconButton.limit.glyph: Several icons overlap by a fixed fraction, tuned for a double arrow. Other pairs may not read as one glyph.
docs.iconButton.limit.icons: It draws the icons of the library only: it takes the name of one, not an SVG of your own.
docs.iconButton.limit.label: The label is a string that you translate: there is no string of the library for it.
docs.iconButton.limit.pressed: A pressed state is not painted: aria-pressed reaches the button but nothing changes on the screen, so a toggle shows its state with a different icon.
docs.iconButton.limit.size: There is one size, and one look: no variants and no loading state.
docs.iconButton.state.focusHint: Reach it with Tab: a ring appears around it.
docs.iconButton.state.hoverHint: Move the pointer over it: a background appears and the icon gains contrast.
docs.iconButton.states.description: The states that IconButton has today. A disabled button is not a loading one: the library has no loading state for it.
docs.iconButton.summary: A square button that holds only an icon, named by its label.
docs.iconButton.tooltip.description: An icon has no text, so show its label as a tooltip too, and let the label alone name the button.
docs.iconButton.tooltip.label: Tooltip and label
docs.iconButton.tooltip.title: With a Tooltip
docs.iconButton.usage.description: Import IconButton, choose an icon and give it a label: with no text on the button, the label is its accessible name.
docs.input.a11y.describedby: The hint and the error are linked with aria-describedby, the error first, so a screen reader says what is wrong before the help. Ids of your own are added after them.
docs.input.a11y.disabled: Disabled and read-only are different. A disabled input leaves the tab order and is not sent; a read-only one keeps the focus and its value can be read, selected and sent, and its dashed border says it cannot be changed.
docs.input.a11y.error: An error sets aria-invalid and does not rely on color: the message is text under the field, and the border changes too.
docs.input.a11y.focus: The focus ring shows with the keyboard and is never removed. Keep it visible if you restyle the input.
docs.input.a11y.label: The label is visible and linked to the input, so it is what a screen reader says and what the user clicks to focus the field. Never leave it out for a placeholder.
docs.input.a11y.placeholder: A placeholder is not a label and is gone once the user types: use it for an example of the value, never for an instruction the user needs.
docs.input.api.ariaDescribedby: Native: ids of other text that describes the input. They are joined after the error and the hint.
docs.input.api.ariaInvalid: Native: error is the only thing that sets it, so a value of your own is overwritten.
docs.input.api.className: Added to the input, after the library's own class names.
docs.input.api.error: The error message. It marks the field as invalid, takes the red style and is announced when it appears.
docs.input.api.fieldClassName: Class name of the container of the field. className goes to the input.
docs.input.api.hint: Permanent help text under the field. The input is described by it.
docs.input.api.id: Native: the label points at it. One is generated when you leave it out.
docs.input.api.label: The visible label of the field. It is what names the input.
docs.input.api.others: Every other attribute of the native input element goes to it as it is: type, name, value, defaultValue, disabled, readOnly, required, placeholder, autoComplete, aria-*, the event handlers and ref. It takes no children.
docs.input.field.api.children: Receives the props that link the control to its label, hint and error (id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid) and returns the control. Spread them on it.
docs.input.field.api.className: Class name of the container of the field.
docs.input.field.api.describedBy: Ids of other text that describes the control. They are joined after the error and the hint.
docs.input.field.api.error: The error message. It marks the control as invalid and is announced when it appears.
docs.input.field.api.hint: Permanent help text under the control.
docs.input.field.api.id: The id of the control. One is generated when you leave it out.
docs.input.field.api.label: The visible label of the control.
docs.input.field.description: Field is what Input is made of: the label, the hint and the error, linked to a control by its id and aria-describedby. Use it for a control of your own.
docs.input.field.label: Plan
docs.input.field.note: The style of the library's text controls is not exported, so the control of a Field is yours to style: here it is the browser's own.
docs.input.field.title: Field
docs.input.limit.control: The style of the control is not exported. A select, a textarea or any other control inside a Field comes unstyled, and Field only links its label, hint and error to it.
docs.input.limit.errorAnnouncement: An error is announced when it appears on a page that is already open. One that is there from the first render may not be announced on its own: it is read with the field, through aria-describedby.
docs.input.limit.native: It is for text: the style is for text controls, so a checkbox, a radio or a file input takes the same box and looks wrong.
docs.input.limit.size: There is one size: 40 px high, and 44 px below 768 px of width. It has no slots for an icon or a button inside it.
docs.input.limit.validation: It does not validate anything. The error is the text you pass, and when to show it is up to you.
docs.input.state.disabledHint: It is not focusable and a form does not send its value.
docs.input.state.focusHint: Reach it with Tab: a ring appears around it.
docs.input.state.readOnlyHint: It takes the focus, its value can be selected and a form sends it.
docs.input.states.description: The states that Input has today. Disabled and read-only are two different states: they look and behave in different ways.
docs.input.states.note: There is no loading state: the library has none for an input.
docs.input.summary: A text input with its visible label, its hint and its error, linked to it.
docs.input.usage.description: Import Input and give it a label: the label is visible, and it is what names the input. A hint and an error are linked to it for screen readers.
docs.tooltip.a11y.content: A tooltip is a description, not a place for what the user needs: the page has to say the same thing without it, and the tooltip holds no controls.
docs.tooltip.a11y.describe: While it is open the trigger is described by the tooltip through aria-describedby. When the tooltip repeats the accessible name, as it does on an IconButton, turn describe off.
docs.tooltip.a11y.dialog: Inside a Dialog the first Escape closes only the tooltip. The second one closes the dialog, and the focus goes back to what opened it.
docs.tooltip.a11y.dismiss: Escape closes it and the focus stays where it was. It stays closed until the pointer or the focus come back, so it never blocks what is under it for good.
docs.tooltip.a11y.hover: The pointer can travel from the trigger onto the tooltip without closing it, and it stays open until the pointer leaves or the user dismisses it: it can be dismissed, the pointer can rest on it and it is persistent (WCAG 1.4.13).
docs.tooltip.a11y.keyboard: It opens when the trigger receives the focus, and not only on hover, so a keyboard user reads it. It closes when the focus leaves.
docs.tooltip.a11y.trigger: The trigger has to take the focus (a button, a link, an input). A tooltip on an element that cannot be focused has no way in for the keyboard.
docs.tooltip.api.children: Receives the props of the trigger and returns the trigger element. Spread all of them on it: they are listed below.
docs.tooltip.api.content: What the tooltip says. Keep it short, and put no controls in it.
docs.tooltip.api.describe: Links the text of the tooltip to the trigger as its description. Turn it off when the accessible name of the trigger is already that text, so a screen reader does not say it twice.
docs.tooltip.api.disabled: Suppresses the tooltip, for example while the trigger has a menu open: a tooltip that stays open takes the first Escape, and the menu would not close.
docs.tooltip.api.placement: The side of the trigger where the tooltip appears. It flips to another side when it does not fit in the window.
docs.tooltip.dialog.tip: Saves the name and closes the dialog.
docs.tooltip.dialog.title: Save the name
docs.tooltip.limit.delay: It opens as soon as the pointer or the focus arrive, and there is no prop to delay it. It closes 120 ms after the pointer leaves.
docs.tooltip.limit.dialog: Do not put it on the control that takes the first focus of a Dialog: it opens while the dialog moves in and ends a few pixels from its trigger. Put another control first.
docs.tooltip.limit.interactive: It is not a popover: the pointer can reach it, but it holds no controls, and it closes when the pointer and the focus have left.
docs.tooltip.limit.placement: There are three placements. The tooltip flips when it does not fit, but there is no way to ask for another side, an offset or an arrow.
docs.tooltip.limit.spread: What you spread replaces the ref, the four handlers and the aria-describedby of the trigger. Call your own handlers from inside the ones that Tooltip gives you, and join the ids of a description of your own.
docs.tooltip.limit.touch: It has been tried with the pointer and the keyboard, and not on touch screens, which have no hover. Check how it behaves there, and do not make it the only place that says something.
docs.tooltip.pattern.dialogHint: Open the dialog, Tab to its last button to open the tooltip and press Escape twice: the tooltip closes first, then the dialog.
docs.tooltip.patterns.description: The two uses that need more than a trigger and a text: on a button that has only an icon, and inside a Dialog.
docs.tooltip.patterns.title: Patterns
docs.tooltip.placement.description: The side of the trigger where the tooltip appears. It flips to another side when the window has no room.
docs.tooltip.placement.title: Placement
docs.tooltip.state.disabledHint: The tooltip never opens, and the button works as usual.
docs.tooltip.state.escapeHint: Open it with Tab and press Escape: the tooltip closes and the focus stays on the button.
docs.tooltip.state.keyboardHint: Reach the button with Tab: the tooltip opens with the focus.
docs.tooltip.state.pointerHint: Move the pointer over the button: the tooltip opens, and stays while the pointer is on the button or on the tooltip.
docs.tooltip.states.description: A tooltip opens with the pointer and with the keyboard, and Escape closes it. Each of these is the live component: try it.
docs.tooltip.summary: A short description of a control, shown on hover and on keyboard focus.
docs.tooltip.trigger.ariaDescribedby: The id of the tooltip while it is open and describe is on, and nothing while it is closed.
docs.tooltip.trigger.onBlur: Closes the tooltip when the trigger loses the focus.
docs.tooltip.trigger.onFocus: Opens the tooltip when the trigger receives the focus.
docs.tooltip.trigger.onPointerEnter: Opens the tooltip when the pointer enters the trigger.
docs.tooltip.trigger.onPointerLeave: Closes the tooltip after a short delay when the pointer leaves, so that the pointer can travel onto the tooltip.
docs.tooltip.trigger.ref: Registers the trigger as the anchor that the tooltip is placed against. It replaces a ref of your own: merge them yourself.
docs.tooltip.trigger.title: What Tooltip hands to its trigger: TooltipTriggerProps
docs.tooltip.usage.description: Import Tooltip and spread what it gives you on the element that triggers it. The text is a description: the control has to make sense without it.
